dependency_coverage.name: Bool
dependency_coverage.meaning: The two-valued Boolean type, whose values are false and true.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Each random variable B_i is Boolean-valued, so its true value can be used as a success indicator.

dependency_coverage.name: Bool.instMeasurableSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: The measurable space on Bool is the top measurable space, so every subset of Bool is measurable.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Laws and measurability of the Boolean-valued functions are interpreted using the full discrete sigma-algebra on Bool.

dependency_coverage.name: Bool.true
dependency_coverage.meaning: The Boolean value true.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The sum in the tail event counts exactly those indices for which B_i(omega) is true.

dependency_coverage.name: DivInvMonoid.toDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: The division operation supplied by a division-inverse monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the quotient (e times the parameter sum) divided by t ordinary real division.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Propositional equality between two terms of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It tests whether B_i(omega) equals true in the indicator defining the count.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: The finite sum of a function over a finite set in an additive commutative monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms both the total parameter S = sum_i p_i and the realized success count sum_i 1_{B_i=true}.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: The finite set containing every element of a finite type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Both sums range over every index i in the finite index type.

dependency_coverage.name: Fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: A type equipped with a finite enumeration of all its elements.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The index set is finite, although it is not required to be nonempty.

dependency_coverage.name: HDiv.hDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous division operation selected by a division typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real arguments it denotes the real quotient (e S) / t in the bound.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous multiplication operation selected by a multiplication typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real arguments it denotes the products e S and exp(-S) times ((e S)/t)^t.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous exponentiation operation selected by a power typeclass.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With real base and real exponent it raises (e S)/t to the real power t.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The non-strict order relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses p_i <= 1, the upper-tail event t <= the success count, and the final probability upper bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The strict order relation supplied by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It imposes the strict threshold condition S < t.

dependency_coverage.name: Measurable
dependency_coverage.meaning: A function is measurable when the preimage of every measurable target set is measurable.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Every Boolean-valued function B_i is explicitly assumed measurable.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasurableSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: A sigma-algebra structure specifying the measurable subsets of a type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It equips the sample type Omega with the measurable structure used by mu, the laws, independence, and measurability assumptions.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure
dependency_coverage.meaning: The property that a measure has total mass one.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires mu to be a probability measure on Omega.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure
dependency_coverage.meaning: A countably additive nonnegative extended-real-valued measure on a measurable space.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The object mu measures the tail event and also determines the laws and independence of the B_i.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real-valued conversion of the extended nonnegative measure of a set.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The left side is the real number obtained from mu of the upper-tail event; because mu is a probability measure, this is its ordinary real probability.

dependency_coverage.name: NNReal
dependency_coverage.meaning: The subtype of real numbers that are nonnegative.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Every parameter p_i is automatically nonnegative, and hp additionally bounds it above by one.

dependency_coverage.name: NNReal.toReal
dependency_coverage.meaning: The coercion extracting the underlying real number from a nonnegative real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It embeds each p_i into the real sum S appearing in the threshold condition and exponential bound.

dependency_coverage.name: Neg.neg
dependency_coverage.meaning: The unary negation operation supplied by a Neg instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms -S in the factor exp(-S).

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The interpretation of a natural-number literal in a target numeric type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the literals zero and one used for the parameter bound and real-valued indicators.

dependency_coverage.name: One.toOfNat1
dependency_coverage.meaning: The mechanism interpreting the numeral 1 from a type's multiplicative-one operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It identifies the upper parameter bound as 1 in NNReal and the success indicator value as 1 in Real.

dependency_coverage.name: PMF.bernoulli
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a nonnegative real p <= 1, the probability mass function on Bool assigning mass p to true and 1-p to false.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The law assumption says B_i is a Bernoulli Boolean variable with success probability p_i.

dependency_coverage.name: PMF.toMeasure
dependency_coverage.meaning: The probability measure induced by a probability mass function on a measurable discrete type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It converts the Bernoulli mass function into the measure that is asserted to be the distribution of B_i.

dependency_coverage.name: PartialOrder.toPreorder
dependency_coverage.meaning: The preorder obtained by forgetting antisymmetry from a partial order.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It participates only in selecting the standard order used to state p_i <= 1.

dependency_coverage.name: Preorder.toLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The non-strict comparison operation underlying a preorder.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes hp the standard NNReal inequality p_i <= 1.

dependency_coverage.name: ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw
dependency_coverage.meaning: The assertion that a measurable-space-valued function, under a specified source measure, has a specified pushforward probability law.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For each i, it asserts that the distribution of B_i under mu is the Bernoulli measure with parameter p_i.

dependency_coverage.name: ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun
dependency_coverage.meaning: Indexed mutual independence of a family of measurable-space-valued functions with respect to a measure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires the entire finite family (B_i)_i to be mutually independent under mu.

dependency_coverage.name: Real

dependency_coverage.name: Real.exp
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real exponential function.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies exp(-S) and exp(1) = e in the Chernoff-type bound.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instDivInvMonoid

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual non-strict order on the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the assumption S < t as the usual strict real inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual multiplication operation on the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instNeg
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual additive negation operation on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the exponent in exp(-S) the ordinary negative of S.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instOne
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual real number one.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies exp(1) and the value one for a true success indicator.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real exponentiation of a real base by a real exponent, implemented as Real.rpow.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual real number zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0

dependency_coverage.name: instOneNNReal
dependency_coverage.meaning: The multiplicative identity one in the nonnegative real numbers.

dependency_coverage.meaning: The set consisting of exactly the elements satisfying a predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the event of outcomes omega whose success count is at least t.

binders: A finite (possibly empty) index type I.
A sample type Omega equipped with a measurable space.
A probability measure mu on Omega.
A family of Boolean-valued functions B_i : Omega -> Bool indexed by i in I.
A family of nonnegative-real parameters p_i indexed by i in I.
hypotheses: For every i, p_i <= 1 (and p_i >= 0 because p_i is a nonnegative real).
The indexed family (B_i)_i is mutually independent under mu.
For every i, the law of B_i under mu is the Boolean Bernoulli law with probability p_i of true and probability 1-p_i of false.
For every i, B_i is measurable.
Writing S = sum_{i in I} p_i as a real number, S < t.
conclusions: The real probability mu({omega : t <= sum_{i in I} 1_{B_i(omega)=true}}) is at most exp(-S) * ((exp(1) * S) / t)^t, where the exponentiation is real exponentiation.
mathematical_definitions: S := sum_{i in I} p_i, with each nonnegative-real p_i viewed as a real.
X(omega) := sum_{i in I} (1 if B_i(omega) = true, and 0 otherwise), a real-valued count of true outcomes.
The tail event is {omega in Omega : t <= X(omega)}.
The right-hand side is e^{-S} (e S / t)^t, using Real.rpow for the real power.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any finite family of mutually independent Boolean Bernoulli random variables B_i with respective success probabilities p_i in [0,1] on a probability space, let S be the sum of the p_i. If the real threshold t is strictly larger than S, then the probability that the number of true outcomes is at least t is bounded above by e^{-S}(eS/t)^t, with the last power interpreted as real exponentiation.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index type is only assumed finite and may be empty; there is no nonemptiness assumption.
The variables are specifically Bool-valued, and success is specifically the value true; this is not stated for arbitrary real-valued Bernoulli encodings.
Each p_i is an NNReal and is separately assumed <= 1, so the parameter range is [0,1].
The threshold t is an arbitrary real, not necessarily an integer. Since S is nonnegative and S < t, the hypotheses force t > 0.
The conclusion concerns the non-strict upper-tail event X >= t (encoded as t <= X).
The power on the right is Real.rpow with real exponent t; edge cases therefore follow the library semantics of real power rather than an integer power convention.
When S = 0, the base (e S)/t is zero and t > 0; the bound uses the library's value for 0 raised to a positive real power.
The explicit measurability assumptions are redundant at the level of the discrete top measurable space on Bool but remain premises of the proposition.
The statement gives only this one-sided upper-tail probability bound and does not encode a lower-tail or two-sided estimate.
